terra.problem: The explanation connects the slain directly to the city's violence, but the text does not identify whose violence caused these deaths.
Saying he will not joke comments on how he is telling the passage.
The joke about a confused betrayer makes light of the serious betrayal described in the passage.
The verse names nations and kingdoms as the audience; it does not say nobody is left out.
The passage asks who will grieve and where comforters can be found. It does not state that nobody mourns.
The passage asks who will grieve; it does not state that nobody steps up to mourn.
Identifying Edom and Moab as nations brings in a Bible fact from outside the passage without a reference.
Identifying Persia and Media as nations brings in a Bible fact from outside the passage without a reference.
This calls the passage heavy again after both explanations for card 4 have already done so.
This calls the passage heavy again after both explanations for card 4 have already done so.
Seeking refuge does not establish that Nineveh is not planning a comeback.
The explanation says the figs need no effort, but the picture says they fall when the trees are shaken.
The verse says the gates are open and their bars consumed by fire, not that the gates are unguarded.

The explanation says the locusts take everything and asserts that the locust is a picture of the merchants. The text says the locust strips the land, but leaves the connection to the merchants unstated.
The passage does not say the locusts leave too quickly to do anything to the walls.
Being scattered does not establish that the people are not sitting down.
The earlier question asks who will grieve for Nineveh; this verse does not state that nobody grieves.
The text says those who hear applaud; it does not say nobody comes to help.
Experiencing the king's cruelty does not establish that everyone knew him.
